report:
# Conclusion

The claim that taking ibuprofen worsens COVID-19 is not supported by evidence. Your skepticism is well-founded.

## Origin of the Claim

The concern began in March 2020 when French Health Minister Olivier Véran tweeted that anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen could worsen COVID-19. This was amplified by a Lancet Respiratory Medicine letter by Fang et al. hypothesizing that NSAIDs might upregulate ACE2 receptors, potentially increasing SARS-CoV-2 entry into cells. The WHO initially cautioned against ibuprofen but reversed course within days, stating it does not recommend against its use.

## What the Evidence Shows

- **FDA**: "At this time, FDA is not aware of scientific evidence connecting the use of NSAIDs, like ibuprofen, with worsening COVID-19 symptoms." (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-alerts-and-statements/fda-advises-patients-use-non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory-drugs-nsaids-covid-19)

- **WHO**: Clarified there is no evidence ibuprofen worsens COVID-19. (https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ibuprofen-covid-19-novel-coronavirus-1.5501496)

- **Nationwide cohort study**: Found no significant association between ibuprofen prescription claims and severe COVID-19 outcomes (ICU admission, respiratory failure, or death). (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7537121/)

- **Narrative review (2023)**: Concluded "NSAIDs do not increase susceptibility to infection, nor worsen disease outcomes in patients with COVID-19." (https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s10787-023-01309-7.pdf)

## Bottom Line

The original warning was based on anecdotal reports and a mechanistic hypothesis, not clinical data. Subsequent observational studies, systematic reviews, and guidance from major health agencies have found no evidence that ibuprofen worsens COVID-19. Some authorities suggest acetaminophen as a first choice, but ibuprofen is not contraindicated.
